title: ESP32 sensor development board
summary: A compact ESP32-WROOM-32E development board powered and programmed over USB-C, with an on-board BME280 environmental sensor, a status LED, a user button, and a Qwiic expansion connector. The firmware serves temperature, humidity, and pressure as JSON over Wi-Fi.

origin.idea: Design a new ESP32 development board with Wi-Fi, sensors, power management, schematic, PCB, firmware and a complete engineering development pack.

requirements.text: Use an ESP32 module with Wi-Fi and Bluetooth.
Measure temperature, humidity, and pressure with an on-board sensor.
Program and debug over one USB-C cable, with automatic reset into the bootloader.
Power from USB-C 5 V and regulate 3.3 V with headroom for Wi-Fi transmit peaks (at least 500 mA).
Provide a status LED and a user button.
The firmware reads the sensor and serves the readings over Wi-Fi.
Protect the USB data lines against electrostatic discharge.
Offer a 3.3 V Qwiic (I2C) expansion connector.
Board outline no larger than 55 × 28 mm on a 2-layer PCB.
Keep the module antenna keep-out area free of copper.

assumptions.text: No battery: the board runs from USB power only.
The Arduino framework on PlatformIO is acceptable for the first firmware.

questions.question: Should the board run from a battery?
questions.why: A battery adds a charger, a power path, and changes the regulator choice.

questions.question: What supply voltage range must the board accept?
questions.why: It decides between an LDO and a buck regulator.

// Pin assignments for the ESP32 sensor development board (ESP32-WROOM-32E).
// Keep this file identical to the pin map in docs/PCB_SPECIFICATION.md.
#ifndef BOARD_PINS_H
#define BOARD_PINS_H

#define PIN_BOOT_BUTTON 0   // BOOT button to GND (strapping pin: released = normal boot)
#define PIN_UART0_TX 1      // To CP2102N RXD (flashing and console)
#define PIN_UART0_RX 3      // From CP2102N TXD
#define PIN_USER_BUTTON 13  // User button to GND, internal pull-up
#define PIN_I2C_SDA 21      // BME280 and Qwiic connector
#define PIN_I2C_SCL 22      // BME280 and Qwiic connector
#define PIN_LED_STATUS 25   // Green status LED through 1 kOhm to GND
#define PIN_VBUS_SENSE 34   // USB VBUS through a 100k/100k divider (ADC1, input only)

#endif  // BOARD_PINS_H

artifacts.content:
# PCB specification: ESP32 sensor development board

Status: **specification for an EDA tool** (KiCad or Altium). It is not a schematic or a layout, and nothing here has been reviewed by an engineer or built.

## 1. Board summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Module | ESP32-WROOM-32E-N4 (4 MB flash, PCB antenna) |
| Size | 55 × 28 mm, 2 layers, 1.6 mm FR-4, 1 oz copper |
| Power | USB-C 5 V (VBUS) → AP2112K-3.3 LDO → 3.3 V |
| Programming | CP2102N USB-UART with DTR/RTS auto-reset (two MMBT3904) |
| Sensor | Bosch BME280 on I2C, address 0x76 |
| Expansion | Qwiic connector (I2C, 3.3 V), 2 × 10 pin headers at 2.54 mm |

## 2. Power tree

- USB-C VBUS (5 V) → USBLC6-2SC6 (ESD on D+/D−) and a 5.1 kΩ pull-down on each CC pin (sink role).
- VBUS → AP2112K-3.3TRG1 (600 mA) → 3V3 rail. Input 10 µF, output 10 µF + 0.1 µF at the module.
- ESP32 Wi-Fi transmit peaks reach about 500 mA: keep the 3V3 trace ≥ 0.5 mm and add a 22 µF bulk capacitor close to the module.
- LDO dissipation at 5 V → 3.3 V and 0.5 A is about 0.85 W in bursts: give the SOT-23-5 a copper pour on both layers with vias (see risk K1).

## 3. Pin map

| GPIO | Signal | Connected to | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | BOOT_BUTTON | SW2 to GND, auto-reset Q2 | Strapping pin: must be high at reset for normal boot (10 kΩ pull-up inside the module) |
| 1 | UART0_TX | CP2102N RXD | Flashing and console |
| 3 | UART0_RX | CP2102N TXD | Flashing and console |
| 13 | USER_BUTTON | SW3 to GND | Internal pull-up |
| 21 | I2C_SDA | BME280 SDA, Qwiic | 4.7 kΩ pull-up to 3V3 |
| 22 | I2C_SCL | BME280 SCL, Qwiic | 4.7 kΩ pull-up to 3V3 |
| 25 | LED_STATUS | D1 through 1 kΩ | Active high |
| 34 | VBUS_SENSE | 100 kΩ / 100 kΩ divider from VBUS | ADC1, input only |
| EN | RESET | SW1 to GND, auto-reset Q1, 10 kΩ pull-up, 1 µF to GND | |

## 4. Layout rules

- Antenna keep-out: no copper, traces, or components under or within 15 mm in front of the module antenna; place the module at the board edge with the antenna overhanging or over a cut-out (ESP32-WROOM-32E datasheet, PCB layout section).
- Continuous ground plane on the bottom layer; stitch with vias around the module's GND pads.
- USB D+/D− as a 90 Ω differential pair, short and away from the antenna.
- Decoupling capacitors within 2 mm of their supply pins.

## 5. Manufacturing notes

- Fabrication: JLCPCB/PCBWay standard 2-layer process, HASL lead-free, green solder mask.
- Assembly: all parts on the top side; the module is the heaviest part and is placed last by hand if needed.
- Test points on 3V3, VBUS, GND, EN, GPIO0, TXD, RXD.

artifacts.purpose: How each requirement will be verified.
artifacts.content:
# Test plan: ESP32 sensor development board

Every test below is **planned**: none has been run. Record results here as you run them.

| Test | Verifies | Method | Tool | Procedure | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | R6 | Build | PlatformIO | cd firmware && pio run -e esp32dev | Not run |
| T2 | R4 | Bench test | Bench supply, oscilloscope | Power from USB-C; measure 3V3 during Wi-Fi transmit; ripple and droop must stay within 3.0–3.6 V | Not run |
| T3 | R3 | Bench test | PlatformIO, USB-C cable | Upload firmware without pressing buttons; auto-reset must enter the bootloader | Not run |
| T4 | R2 | Bench test | Reference thermometer/hygrometer | Compare readings after 10 minutes of warm-up | Not run |
| T5 | R10 | Inspection | EDA tool | Check the antenna keep-out area on all copper layers | Not run |
| T6 | R7 | Review | EDA tool | USBLC6 placed next to J1, D+/D− routed through it | Not run |
| T7 | R1, R6 | Bench test | Phone or laptop on the same Wi-Fi | Open http://board-ip/readings; JSON updates every 2 s | Not run |
| T8 | R5 | Bench test | — | LED blinks while connecting; holding USER at power-up enters Wi-Fi setup | Not run |
| T9 | R8 | Inspection | Qwiic cable, known Qwiic sensor | Pin order GND, 3V3, SDA, SCL; device appears on an I2C scan | Not run |
| T10 | R9 | Inspection | EDA tool | Board outline 55 × 28 mm, two layers | Not run |

# ESP32 sensor development board

An example engineering project from Git Architecture Diagram's "Start from an Idea" workspace. The design, firmware, and documents are proposals: they have structural and rule checks (see the validation report) but have not been built, compiled, or tested.

- firmware/: PlatformIO project (Arduino framework). Build with `pio run -e esp32dev`.
- docs/PCB_SPECIFICATION.md: the hardware specification to capture in an EDA tool.
- hardware/bom.csv: bill of materials.
- docs/TEST_PLAN.md: how each requirement will be verified.

validationPlan.title: 3V3 rail under Wi-Fi transmit
validationPlan.procedure: Measure 3V3 droop during Wi-Fi bursts; stay within 3.0–3.6 V.

validationPlan.title: Antenna keep-out
validationPlan.procedure: Check every copper layer under and in front of the antenna.

validationPlan.title: ESD protection placement
validationPlan.procedure: USBLC6 next to J1 with D+/D− routed through it.

validationPlan.title: Readings over Wi-Fi
validationPlan.procedure: Open http://board-ip/readings and watch the values update.

validationPlan.title: LED and button
validationPlan.procedure: LED blinks while connecting; holding USER at power-up enters Wi-Fi setup.

validationPlan.title: Qwiic pin order and bus
validationPlan.procedure: GND, 3V3, SDA, SCL; device found by an I2C scan.

risks.text: LDO dissipation reaches about 0.85 W during Wi-Fi bursts.
risks.mitigation: Copper pour with vias under the regulator; move to a buck regulator if the board gets warm in T2.

risks.text: An enclosure or nearby copper can detune the PCB antenna.
risks.mitigation: Respect the keep-out (T5) and test range in the final enclosure.

risks.text: GPIO0 is a strapping pin shared with the BOOT button and the auto-reset circuit.
risks.mitigation: Keep the module's pull-up and avoid other loads on GPIO0.
